FINAL RORK REMOVAL AUDIT AND MIGRATION MAP
TARGET: 0% RORK API / SDK / RUNTIME DEPENDENCY IN IVX

OWNER DECISION

IVX must operate independently from Rork.

Rork may perform this cleanup task, but the final production platform must not require any Rork-owned:

- API
- SDK
- package
- runtime
- proxy
- authentication service
- deployment service
- database
- storage
- analytics
- telemetry
- error reporting
- update service
- build service
- generated secret
- domain
- subdomain
- webhook
- worker
- queue
- repository
- account
- application identifier
- code-signing identity

Do not remove legitimate IVX source code only because Rork originally generated it.

The requirement is:

IVX owns and controls the code, infrastructure, credentials, repositories, services, and deployment flow.

Do not mark PASS based only on a text search.

Prove the result using:

SOURCE SCAN
DEPENDENCY SCAN
NETWORK SCAN
BUILD SCAN
RUNTIME SCAN
INFRASTRUCTURE SCAN
PRODUCTION VERIFICATION

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE CURRENT PRODUCTION
==================================================

Before changing anything, record:

- GitHub repository
- Branch
- GitHub HEAD SHA
- Render API service ID
- Render worker service ID
- Current API deployment ID
- Current worker deployment ID
- Current website deployment ID
- Live API SHA
- Live worker SHA
- Website version
- Database migration version
- Current rollback SHA
- UTC timestamp

Verify:

- https://ivxholding.com
- https://api.ivxholding.com/health
- https://api.ivxholding.com/version
- Public chat
- Owner login
- Worker status

Create a safe rollback point.

Do not start removal without recording this baseline.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — CREATE THE COMPLETE IVX OWNERSHIP MAP
==================================================

Create a map of every IVX system component.

For each component, return:

- Component name
- Purpose
- Source directory
- Repository
- Owner account
- Provider
- Service ID
- Domain
- Environment-variable names
- Dependencies
- Production status
- Rork dependency: YES / NO / UNKNOWN
- Migration required: YES / NO
- Evidence

Map at minimum:

1. Mobile application
2. Web application
3. Landing website
4. Backend API
5. Public chat
6. Owner chat
7. Autonomous worker
8. Deployment authorization
9. Proof ledger
10. Job queue
11. Supabase database
12. Supabase authentication
13. Supabase storage
14. Realtime
15. Render services
16. GitHub repositories
17. AWS services
18. DNS
19. Email
20. SMS
21. Notifications
22. Analytics
23. Error reporting
24. Media processing
25. File uploads
26. Android builds
27. iOS builds
28. Environment groups
29. Secrets management
30. Monitoring
31. Backups
32. Rollback system
33. Treasury
34. Accounting
35. Members
36. Investors
37. Buyers
38. Properties
39. Deals
40. Reels

==================================================
PHASE 3 — SEARCH THE ENTIRE SOURCE TREE
==================================================

Scan every tracked and relevant untracked source file.

Search case-insensitively for:

rork
rork.com
api.rork.com
rork.app
rork.dev
rork-sdk
rork_sdk
rork-api
rork_api
rork-client
rork_client
rork-runtime
rork_runtime
rork-proxy
rork_proxy
rork-auth
rork_auth
rork-ai
rork_ai
rork-deploy
rork_deploy
rork-update
rork_update
rork-generated
rork_project
rorkProject
rorkProjectId
RORK_API_KEY
RORK_TOKEN
RORK_SECRET
RORK_PROJECT_ID
RORK_BASE_URL
RORK_ENDPOINT

Scan:

- TypeScript
- JavaScript
- TSX
- JSX
- Swift
- Kotlin
- Java
- Objective-C
- JSON
- YAML
- TOML
- XML
- Gradle files
- Podfiles
- Dockerfiles
- Shell scripts
- SQL
- Environment templates
- CI/CD files
- Lockfiles
- Native project files
- Expo configuration
- EAS configuration
- Build scripts
- Documentation used by automation

For every result, classify it as:

A. Active production dependency
B. Active development dependency
C. Inactive legacy configuration
D. Documentation-only reference
E. Human-readable project name
F. False positive

Return:

- File
- Line
- Exact reference
- Classification
- Removal action
- Replacement
- Verification status

Do not hide references because they are in generated or native files.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — DEPENDENCY AND LOCKFILE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit all package manifests and lockfiles:

- package.json
- bun.lock
- bun.lockb
- package-lock.json
- yarn.lock
- pnpm-lock.yaml
- Podfile
- Podfile.lock
- build.gradle
- settings.gradle
- gradle.properties
- libs.versions.toml
- Package.swift
- Gemfile
- Gemfile.lock

Inspect:

- Direct dependencies
- Transitive dependencies
- Git-based dependencies
- Private registries
- Postinstall scripts
- Prepare scripts
- Binary downloads
- Build plugins
- Native modules
- Expo config plugins

Return a dependency table:

- Package
- Version
- Direct/transitive
- Registry/source
- Owner/publisher
- Used by file
- Rork-owned: YES / NO / UNKNOWN
- Removal required
- Replacement
- Test status

Acceptance:

- No Rork-owned package remains.
- No dependency downloads code or binaries from a Rork domain.
- No postinstall script contacts Rork.
- No private Rork registry remains.
- Lockfiles are regenerated after removal.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — EXPO AND REACT NATIVE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

- app.json
- app.config.js
- app.config.ts
- eas.json
- metro.config.js
- babel.config.js
- expo-env.d.ts
- Expo Router configuration
- Native plugins
- Update configuration
- Runtime version
- Project ID
- Bundle identifiers
- Android application ID
- Deep-link scheme
- Universal links
- Associated domains
- OTA update URL
- Asset URLs
- Build profiles

Confirm:

- No Rork Expo project ID
- No Rork EAS owner
- No Rork OTA update endpoint
- No Rork runtime URL
- No Rork application identifier
- No Rork deep-link scheme
- No Rork domain in associated links
- No Rork credentials required to build

Return the exact owner account used for Expo/EAS.

If EAS is used, prove it belongs to the IVX-controlled account.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — IOS NATIVE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

- Bundle identifier
- Team identifier
- Provisioning profile
- Signing certificate
- Entitlements
- Associated domains
- URL schemes
- Info.plist
- Privacy manifest
- Swift packages
- CocoaPods
- Build phases
- Run scripts
- API base URLs
- Analytics configuration
- Push-notification configuration

Verify:

- No Rork signing identity
- No Rork Apple team
- No Rork bundle identifier
- No Rork associated domain
- No Rork SDK
- No Rork build script
- No Rork telemetry
- No Rork update service

Do not perform App Store submission now.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — ANDROID NATIVE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

- namespace
- applicationId
- signingConfig
- keystore ownership
- AndroidManifest.xml
- intent filters
- deep links
- network security configuration
- Gradle plugins
- Maven repositories
- Firebase configuration
- API URLs
- native modules
- release build scripts

Verify:

- No Rork package namespace
- No Rork Maven registry
- No Rork signing key
- No Rork deep link
- No Rork SDK
- No Rork runtime URL
- No Rork build dependency

Do not expose keystore values.

Return only ownership and verification status.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — BACKEND SOURCE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit the entire backend, including:

- API routes
- Middleware
- Authentication
- Worker services
- Chat services
- Deployment clients
- Internal authorization
- Webhooks
- Queues
- Scheduled jobs
- AI provider clients
- Media services
- Email/SMS clients
- Monitoring
- Error reporting
- Proof ledger
- Health/version routes

Identify all outbound network requests.

For every outbound request return:

- Source file
- Function
- Destination hostname
- HTTP method
- Purpose
- Authentication type
- Production use
- Rork-owned destination: YES / NO
- Replacement required

Acceptance:

- Zero outbound production traffic to Rork.
- Zero Rork proxy between IVX and any provider.
- IVX calls approved providers directly.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE AUDIT
==================================================

Audit variable names across:

- Render API
- Render worker
- Render environment groups
- Expo/EAS
- Local templates
- GitHub Actions
- AWS
- Supabase functions
- Native build configuration

Return names and status only. Never reveal values.

Classify every variable:

- IVX-owned
- Provider-owned
- Rork-owned
- Legacy
- Unknown
- Unused

Search specifically for variables containing:

RORK
RORK_API
RORK_TOKEN
RORK_SECRET
RORK_PROJECT
RORK_URL
RORK_PROXY
RORK_AUTH
RORK_DEPLOY
RORK_UPDATE

For every Rork or unknown variable:

- Identify reader file/function
- Prove whether runtime reads it
- Replace or remove it
- Restart affected service
- Verify startup

Acceptance:

- Zero active Rork environment variables.
- Zero unknown variables required for production startup.
- No valid IVX credentials are deleted.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — DOMAIN AND NETWORK AUDIT
==================================================

Create an allowlist of approved production destinations.

Expected approved providers may include only verified IVX services such as:

- ivxholding.com
- api.ivxholding.com
- Supabase project domains
- Render service domains
- GitHub
- AWS
- Approved AI provider
- Approved email provider
- Approved SMS provider
- Approved monitoring provider
- Expo/EAS if IVX-controlled

Do not assume the list is correct; verify actual use.

Inspect:

- Browser requests
- Mobile requests
- Backend egress
- Worker egress
- WebSocket connections
- DNS lookups
- Redirects
- Image/video hosts
- Upload destinations
- Analytics calls
- Crash-reporting calls
- OTA update checks

Run production network captures for:

1. Website startup
2. Owner login
3. Public chat
4. Owner chat
5. Member registration
6. Image upload
7. Video upload
8. Reels playback
9. Worker health
10. QA-only autonomous job
11. Android app startup
12. iOS app startup where available

Acceptance:

- No request resolves to a Rork domain.
- No redirect passes through Rork.
- No Rork WebSocket remains open.
- No Rork analytics or telemetry event is transmitted.
- No Rork CDN hosts production assets.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — GITHUB AND CI/CD OWNERSHIP AUDIT
==================================================

Verify:

- Repository is under the owner-controlled GitHub account.
- Main branch is owner-controlled.
- Required branch protections are documented.
- GitHub Actions use IVX-controlled secrets.
- No Rork GitHub App is required.
- No Rork bot has required write access.
- No deploy key belongs exclusively to Rork.
- No webhook calls Rork.
- No workflow imports a Rork-owned action.
- No submodule points to Rork.
- No package references a Rork Git repository.

Return:

- Repository
- Owner
- Branch
- Active deploy workflow
- Required GitHub Apps
- Webhooks
- Deploy keys
- Actions
- External collaborators
- Rork dependency: YES / NO

Do not remove collaborators unless the owner explicitly approves access removal.

The app must continue functioning if Rork access is removed.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — RENDER OWNERSHIP AUDIT
==================================================

Audit every Render service:

- API
- Worker
- Background workers
- Cron jobs
- Redis
- Databases
- Static sites
- Environment groups

For each service return:

- Service name
- Service ID
- Workspace owner
- Repository
- Branch
- Root directory
- Build command
- Start command
- Dockerfile
- Health path
- Domains
- Environment groups
- Auto-deploy setting
- Rork dependency

Verify:

- Services belong to the IVX/owner-controlled workspace.
- No Rork workspace is required.
- No Rork-owned deploy hook is required.
- No Rork proxy is in front of the API.
- No Rork-specific build image is used.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — SUPABASE OWNERSHIP AUDIT
==================================================

Verify:

- Project ownership
- Organization ownership
- Project URL
- Authentication configuration
- Storage ownership
- Database ownership
- Edge Functions
- Webhooks
- Extensions
- Realtime
- SMTP configuration
- External OAuth providers
- RLS policies
- Service-role usage

Search all Supabase:

- Functions
- Database functions
- Triggers
- Webhooks
- Vault entries
- Redirect URLs
- Authentication site URLs
- Allowed redirect URLs

Acceptance:

- No Rork webhook.
- No Rork redirect URL.
- No Rork Edge Function dependency.
- No Rork-controlled service account.
- IVX can administer the project without Rork.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — AWS AND DNS AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

- Route 53
- S3
- CloudFront
- EC2
- IAM
- Certificates
- DNS records
- CDN origins
- Buckets
- Webhooks
- Access keys
- Service roles

Verify DNS for:

- ivxholding.com
- www.ivxholding.com
- api.ivxholding.com
- chat.ivxholding.com
- Any additional production subdomain

Acceptance:

- No DNS record points to Rork.
- No CNAME points to a Rork service.
- No Rork account owns an essential AWS resource.
- No production asset requires a Rork bucket or CDN.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — AUTHENTICATION AUDIT
==================================================

Map every authentication type:

- Public user
- Member
- Investor
- Buyer
- Admin
- Owner
- Autonomous worker
- Internal service
- Deployment approval

For each authentication path return:

- Identity provider
- Token issuer
- Token validator
- Middleware file
- Database owner mapping
- Refresh mechanism
- Expiration
- Revocation
- Rork dependency

Acceptance:

- Supabase or another approved IVX provider issues user sessions.
- Internal worker authentication is IVX-owned.
- No Rork service issues or validates production identity.
- Owner approval does not require Rork chat.
- Autonomous execution operates after Rork access is removed.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — AI PROVIDER AUDIT
==================================================

Map every AI call:

- IVX IA chat
- Senior developer worker
- Public chat
- Document analysis
- Image analysis
- Video analysis
- Autonomous planning
- Reports
- Marketing AI
- Investment assistant

For each AI path return:

- Source file
- Model/provider
- Base URL
- Key variable name
- Direct call or proxy
- Rork dependency
- Fallback provider
- Error behavior

Acceptance:

- IVX calls the approved AI provider directly or through an IVX-controlled gateway.
- No Rork AI gateway or proxy remains.
- No Rork account is needed for AI access.
- Model/provider failures produce structured errors.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — ANALYTICS, TELEMETRY, AND ERROR REPORTING
==================================================

Audit:

- Analytics SDKs
- Crash reporting
- Performance monitoring
- Session replay
- Logging
- Remote configuration
- Feature flags
- Push notification analytics

Search for:

- Rork event endpoints
- Rork project IDs
- Rork telemetry headers
- Device identifiers sent to Rork
- Session replay sent to Rork
- Error logs sent to Rork

Acceptance:

- Zero telemetry sent to Rork.
- Zero Rork session replay.
- Zero Rork analytics SDK.
- Monitoring uses an IVX-controlled or approved provider.

==================================================
PHASE 18 — BUILD AND UPDATE PIPELINE
==================================================

Map:

CODE
→ TEST
→ COMMIT
→ PUSH
→ BUILD
→ DEPLOY
→ HEALTH CHECK
→ VERSION CHECK
→ ROLLBACK

For each stage return:

- Tool/provider
- Account owner
- Required credential
- Service
- Evidence
- Rork dependency

Verify:

- Website builds without Rork.
- API builds without Rork.
- Worker builds without Rork.
- Android APK builds without Rork.
- iOS build compiles without Rork.
- Production deployment succeeds without Rork.
- OTA updates, if used, are IVX-controlled.
- Rollback works without Rork.

==================================================
PHASE 19 — REMOVE ACTIVE RORK DEPENDENCIES
==================================================

For each confirmed active Rork dependency:

1. Record the current behavior.
2. Identify the IVX-controlled replacement.
3. Add replacement configuration.
4. Add tests.
5. Migrate the call path.
6. Verify the replacement.
7. Remove Rork code/configuration.
8. Regenerate lockfiles.
9. Remove obsolete variables.
10. Restart affected services.
11. Retest production.
12. Record proof.

Do not delete first and investigate later.

Do not remove a dependency until the replacement passes.

==================================================
PHASE 20 — CLEAN LEGACY REFERENCES
==================================================

After production is independent, remove or rename legacy references where safe:

- Rork package references
- Rork URLs
- Rork environment variables
- Rork telemetry
- Rork project IDs
- Rork build scripts
- Rork webhooks
- Rork update endpoints
- Rork private registries
- Rork generated runtime imports

Repository names containing “rork” may be migrated to an IVX-owned repository name only through a controlled process.

Do not break the active Render repository binding.

If renaming the repository:

1. Create the IVX-named repository under the owner account.
2. Preserve full Git history.
3. Push all branches and tags.
4. Update Render.
5. Update CI/CD.
6. Verify production.
7. Archive the old repository only after successful verification.

A repository name alone is not an active SDK dependency, but it should be documented as legacy branding.

==================================================
PHASE 21 — ADD AUTOMATED RORK-DEPENDENCY GUARD
==================================================

Add a CI security check that fails future builds if active Rork dependencies return.

Scan for:

- Rork domains
- Rork packages
- Rork variables
- Rork source imports
- Rork registries
- Rork webhooks
- Rork deployment hooks
- Rork telemetry endpoints

Allow only explicitly approved documentation or historical migration references.

CI must return:

- PASS when no active dependency exists
- FAIL with file and line when a prohibited dependency appears

==================================================
PHASE 22 — BUILD WITHOUT RORK ACCESS
==================================================

Perform a clean-room verification.

Requirements:

- Fresh checkout from the owner GitHub repository
- No Rork login
- No Rork browser session
- No Rork API token
- No Rork SDK
- No cached Rork package
- No Rork environment variable

Execute:

1. Install dependencies.
2. Run lint.
3. Run type checking.
4. Run unit tests.
5. Run integration tests.
6. Build website.
7. Build backend.
8. Build worker.
9. Build Android APK.
10. Build iOS project where supported.
11. Start API.
12. Start worker.
13. Call /health.
14. Call /version.
15. Run a QA-only worker job.

Acceptance:

- Every required step succeeds without Rork access.

==================================================
PHASE 23 — LIVE PRODUCTION NETWORK PROOF
==================================================

After deployment, capture production traffic again.

Return a hostname table:

- Hostname
- Provider
- Purpose
- Request count
- Approved: YES / NO
- Rork-owned: YES / NO

Required result:

Rork-owned hostnames contacted: 0

Also verify:

- No Rork cookies
- No Rork authorization headers
- No Rork JavaScript
- No Rork native binaries
- No Rork WebSocket
- No Rork background request
- No Rork redirect
- No Rork asset URL

==================================================
PHASE 24 — LIVE END-TO-END QA
==================================================

Verify production after removal:

- Website
- Owner login
- Logout/login
- Session persistence
- Public chat
- Owner chat
- Members
- Investors
- Buyers
- Properties
- Deals
- Reels
- Uploads
- Documents
- Treasury
- Audit jobs
- Autonomous worker
- Worker authorization
- Proof ledger
- Health

- Monitoring
- Rollback
- Android APK
- iOS build readiness

For each test return:

- Test ID
- Expected result
- Actual result
- PASS / FAIL
- Commit SHA
- Screenshot/log
- Timestamp

==================================================
PHASE 25 — FINAL PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

Deploy the verified independent IVX release.

Return:

GITHUB
- Repository:
- Repository owner:
- Branch:
- GitHub HEAD SHA:

WEBSITE
- Production URL:
- Deployment ID:
- Live SHA:

- Active Rork authentication:
- Active Rork deployment dependencies:
- Active Rork telemetry:
- Active Rork build dependencies:

==================================================

==================================================
FINAL PASS CONDITIONS
==================================================

Mark RORK ACTIVE DEPENDENCY = 0% only when:

- No active Rork API remains.
- No active Rork SDK remains.
- No Rork package remains.
- No Rork proxy remains.
- No Rork domain receives production traffic.
- No Rork authentication service remains.
- No Rork deployment service is required.
- No Rork secret is required.
- No Rork webhook remains.
- No Rork telemetry remains.
- No Rork build tool is required.
- Android builds without Rork.
- iOS builds without Rork.
- Website builds without Rork.
- API builds and deploys without Rork.
- Worker operates without Rork.
- Autonomous QA completes without Rork.
- Owner controls IVX repositories and infrastructure.
- Clean-room build passes without a Rork account or session.
- Production network capture shows zero Rork destinations.
- GitHub HEAD, Render live SHA, worker SHA, and /version SHA match.

Do not report 0% merely because no text match was found.

Do not report PASS while any item is UNKNOWN.

Do not delete IVX functionality to reach zero.

Replace, test, deploy, verify, and prove every dependency removal.

0% / NOT YET 0%

FINAL EVIDENCE:
Attach source scan, dependency scan, runtime network scan, deployment IDs, commit SHAs, service IDs, build results, and production test timestamps.
